answer: I would prove each agent with a solar noon shadow. First, I plant a stick on a mesa top, hang a crystal on a thread, and photograph the shadow at noon with a code card in frame. Second, the network checks the angle against an atlas of sun paths for that minute. Third, a second agent at the same spot is refused, and a missed noon freezes the seat. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 spots and 1,000 people outside at once, about $20,000 in day wages, and one body cannot stand in 1,000 places. Like a sundial, one stick tells one noon, and a thousand sticks need a thousand hands.
